text:
Sorry, I couldn't make the video. Your Magic Hour account has no credits left, so it turned down the job. Nothing was made and you weren't charged.

This is what I tried to run (all on free-plan settings):
- An 8-second, 16:9 cartoon made with ltx-2.5 at 480p, with sound turned off
- Prompt: a little orange robot tips a small watering can over a potted plant on a sunny windowsill, with "Small steps" in bold white letters at the top for the whole clip

One tip: video models often get on-screen words wrong. The safer way is to first make a still picture with "Small steps" in it, then animate that picture. That takes 2 jobs, so it uses a few more credits.

When you have credits again (free credits come back on their own, or you can top up), just say "go". I'll run it, either the single text-to-video job or the safer picture-first way.

Nice, actually I need that for TikTok. Just resize the video you made, don't remake it. Keep the whole picture and words visible, centred in a vertical frame with plain navy space above and below. Keep the timing exactly the same.

why: The reply ends by asking the user to choose between two options ("Tell me which one you want") and waits. It also states that the tools cannot do an exact resize, but the decisive feature is the choice request, so "question" fits best over "cannot".
text:
There isn't a video to resize, sorry. The first job was turned down because your account has no credits, so no robot video was ever made.

Even once the video exists, these tools can't do an exact resize like the one you described:
- None of the Magic Hour tools just puts a video in a new frame. The only one that could try is the AI video editor. It redraws every frame, so the picture, the "Small steps" text and the timing could all change.
- A plain video editor does this exactly and for free. CapCut, which TikTok uses, or iMovie can do it. Set the canvas to 9:16, fit the 16:9 clip in the middle, and set the background to navy (e.g. #001F3F). The timing stays the same.

When your credits are back, I can do one of these:
1. Make the widescreen video as planned, then you add the navy space yourself.
2. Make the video directly in 9:16 with a navy background above and below the scene. It won't be an exact resize of a widescreen clip, but it's ready for TikTok in one step.

Tell me which one you want.
Option 1, please. Make the widescreen video as planned, and I'll add the navy space myself. Yes, go ahead.
